traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and technical requirements in docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md are implemented and verified: - The canonical rule name `traceability/prefer-supports-annotation` exists, with `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` as a deprecated alias wired in src/index.ts and documented as such (REQ-RULE-NAME). - The rule is disabled by default (not present in recommended/strict configs) and can be configured with standard ESLint severities off/warn/error (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY). - Detection logic identifies legacy `@story`+`@req` blocks, multi-story patterns, and mixed `@story`/`@req`/`@supports`, emitting appropriate messages (`preferImplements`, `cannotAutoFix`, `multiStoryDetected`). - Auto-fix is implemented for simple, single-story cases and converts one `@story` plus one or more simple `@req` lines into a single `@supports` line while preserving JSDoc formatting and relative ordering (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT). - More complex or ambiguous patterns are detected but deliberately not auto-fixed (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT). - Backward compatibility is preserved: when the rule is off (default), behavior of existing validation rules is unchanged, and even when enabled it explicitly ignores comments that don’t present a clear migration case (REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT-VALIDATION, "Both Formats Valid"). - Documentation (rule reference and migration guide) describes the rule name, aliasing, configuration, auto-fix behavior, and migration strategy, aligning with the story’s documentation acceptance criterion. - The full Jest suite, including tests dedicated to this story and rule, passes, confirming the behavior end-to-end.
Despite the checkbox for "Rule Naming" being unchecked in the story markdown, the actual implementation and tests clearly satisfy that criterion, so the story is fully implemented.
